# Yang--Mills transport chain

| Arrow | Source → target | Manifest gain | Possible loss | Theorem obligation | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| R1 | lattice links → gauge quotient | physical redundancy removed | local sections and topology | measurable quotient, orbit fidelity, Haar/Jacobian control | finite/local results only |
| R2 | quotient fields → blocked variables | scale organization | microscopic locality and boundary state | exact disintegration, retained-state completeness, reconstruction modulus | restricted results only |
| R3 | block family → infinite volume | thermodynamic state | boundary uniformity | tightness, uniqueness/phase selection, uniform correlations | open at weak coupling |
| R4 | cutoff family → continuum Schwinger functional | Euclidean covariance target | regulator-specific normalization | renormalized observable convergence, OS axioms, universality, nontriviality | open in 4D pure YM |
| R5 | Schwinger data → OS Hilbert space | physical time and spectrum | none if hypotheses close | reflection positivity, regularity, dense centered core | conditional theorem |
| R6 | Euclidean rigidity → Hamiltonian gap | spectral interpretation | hidden sectors if core incomplete | uniform recovery-to-spectrum theorem | proved abstractly; physical premises open |

The first open physical implication is R2/R3: obtain a full-measure,
volume- and cutoff-uniform rigidity estimate in physical units without
assuming exponential clustering.  The manuscript does not treat a finite
lattice gap as evidence that R3--R6 have closed.
